summary: Erik Zürcher was a sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his PhD at Leiden University (~1947–1959) and studied under Duyvendak, Bagchi, Demiéville, and Chavannes. He served as Professor of East Asian History at Leiden University from 1961 to 1993.
Erik-Jan Zürcher is a historian. He was educated at Het Rijnlands Lyceum Oegstgeest (~1965–1971) and Leiden University (~1971–1984), where he later held an academic post from ~1997 to 2018.

Ernest Bender was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Temple University (~1937–1941) and the University of Pennsylvania (~1941–1947), where he subsequently served as Professor of Indo-Aryan Languages and Literatures from ~1950 to 1989.

Ernest Fenollosa worked in philosophy and Japanology. He studied at Harvard College (~1870–1874) and the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston (~1877–1878). He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1878–1886), MFA Boston (1890–1896), and the University of Tsukuba (1897).

Ernest John Eitel was a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Tübingen (~1856–1860), he served with the London Missionary Society (~1865–1879) and held a post at the University of Adelaide (~1897–1908).

Ernest Mackay was an archaeologist and Indologist. He was educated at Bristol Grammar School and the University of Bristol, later holding a post at the Department of Antiquities in Mandatory Palestine from ~1919 to 1922.

Ernest Renan was a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and linguistics. He studied at Saint-Sulpice Seminary and Collège de France under Eugène Burnouf. He later worked at the Bibliothèque nationale de France (1851–1860) and the Collège de France (1861).

Ernest Sosa is a philosopher. He studied at the University of Miami (~1957–1961) and the University of Pittsburgh (~1961–1964). He served as a professor at Brown University (~1964–2007) and held a post at Rutgers University in ~2007.

Ernst Curtius was an archaeologist and historian who studied at the universities of Bonn (~1833–1834) and Göttingen (~1834–1837). He held posts at Frederick William University Berlin (~1844–1856), the University of Göttingen (~1856–1868), and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1868–1896).

Ernst Gombrich worked in art history. Educated at the Theresianum and the University of Vienna (~1928–1933), he held posts at the University of Vienna, the Warburg Institute (~1936–1976), and the University of London (~1959–1976).

Ernst Haas was an Indologist who studied at Bonn, Berlin (under Albrecht Weber), and Tübingen. He held posts at the British Museum from 1866 and at University College London as Professor des Sanskrit from 1875.

Ernst Kuhn worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Berlin, Heidelberg, Tübingen, Leipzig, and Halle-Wittenberg under Albrecht Weber and Rudolf von Roth. He held posts at Heidelberg (~1875–1877) and Munich (~1877–1920).

Ernst Steinkellner is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Vienna under Erich Frauwallner. His posts include the University of Vienna (1962–2004) and director of the Institute for Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.
Ernst Trumpp was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Rudolf von Roth from ~1848 to 1853. He later served as a professor at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich from ~1874 to 1885.

Ernst Waldschmidt was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Göttingen and under Heinrich Lüders, August Hermann Francke, and Albert Grünwedel. He was a member of the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities and taught at Göttingen (~1936–1965).

Ernst Windisch was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Leipzig University under Curtius, Ritschl, Zarncke, and Brockhaus. He held chairs at Heidelberg (1872) and Strasbourg (1875), and served at Leipzig University (1871–1918) and the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft (~1886–1902).

Erwin Rousselle was a scholar of sinology and Buddhist and religious studies. Between 1924 and 1930 he held posts at Peking, National Peking, Tsinghua, and Yenching universities, later becoming an extraordinary professor at Goethe University Frankfurt in 1935.
Esben Andreasen is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Copenhagen and was a visiting researcher at Otani University in 1992.

Eshin Nishimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned his Ph.D. at Kyoto University (~1957–1965), held a post at Carleton College (~1965–1967), and served as director at Hanazono University (~1967–2004).
Esho Kawasaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who has held leadership posts as president (会長) of Kyushu Ryukoku Gakkai and director (所長) of the Buddhist Cultural Institute.
